texts.preamble: Mohammed Sufiyan vs Raju C on 5 April, 2025 Kabc020016692024 Before Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City Scch-17 Present: Sri.KANCHI Mayanna Goutam B.A.L, Ll.M., Member, Mact Xix Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated this the 5th day of April - 2025 Mvc No. 343/2024 Petitioner/S: Sri Mohammed Sufiyan S/o Mohammed Siddiq, Aged about 23 years, R/at: No.25, 1st main road, 2nd west cross, Yeshwanthapura, Bengaluru North, Bengaluru 560022. (By Sri. N R Shivanna, Adv.,) V/s. Respondents: 1. Sri Raju C S/o Chaluvachari, No.773, 2nd main, 4th cross, Hmt Layout, Nelagadarahalli, Scch-17 2 Mvc No.343/2024 Nagasandra, Bengaluru 560073. (By Sri. Prashantha G N, Adv.,) 2. Tata Aig General Ins. Co. Ltd., No.69, 2nd floor, J P & Devi Jambukeshwar Arcade, Miller's road, Bengaluru 560051. (By Sri. Muralidhar Negavar, Adv.,) Judgment
texts.facts: 1 The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act by claiming compensation for the injuries are sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03-01-2024. 2. The petition averments in brief are as under: On 03-01-2024 at about 12.00 a.m.,the petitioner was proceeding by riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA.50.W.3997 along with one pillion rider from Kothanur towards Thanisandra on the extreme left side on Thanisandra service road and when he reached near Saamar International School, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Cab bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, came to his extreme right side ie., wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident. As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Hosmat hospital, wherein he was diagnosed, took treatment and discharged with an advice of regular followup treatment and bed rest. Petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges. Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and working as technical content intern (SME) Data Science at Incanus Technologies Private Limited and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and suffered loss of income. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notices, both the respondents appeared through their respective counsels but the 1st respondent - owner has not filed written statement. Respondent No.2 - insurance company has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No. KA.05.AJ.8953 and the liability of this respondent is any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the policy was valid at the time of accident. Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. Further it has contended that, the respondent No.1 owner has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license and the vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness as on the time of accident and hence violated the policy conditions. It has further denied the cause and manner of accident and contended that the petitioner without wearing helmet has ridden the third party motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and without having valid DL caused the accident. Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it. Further, examined the Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 & 16. On the other hand, the director talent acquisition at Incanus Technologies Pvt Ltd., is examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 and the driver of the offending car is examined as Rw.2. 6.
texts.arguments: The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus: In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 1205-2021 connected with MFA No. 1803-2021 between HDFC Ergo Gen. Ins. Co, Ltd., V/s. Hanumanthappa and Others, wherein it held as follows; "11. Rule 8 of the Rules of the Road Regulations 1989 reads as follows: Caution at road junction: The driver of a motor vehicle shall slow down when approaching at a road intersection, a road junction, pedestrian crossing or a road corner, and shall not enter any such intersection, junction or crossing until he has become aware that he may do so without endangering the safety of persons thereon. Thus, the IMV report and rough sketch establishes the negligence of the driver of the cab and no grounds are made out to consider the contributory negligence as such, in my humble opinion the above quoted judgment relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 is not applicable to the case on hand. 13. Further the RW.2 the driver of the offending cab bearing No. KA-05-AJ-8953 examined as RW.2 who deposed by alleging the negligence of the petitioner. 14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van. In this regard, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 2906-2016 between Sri. Ganesh V/s. Smt. Jayalakshmi B. Hedge and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that as the injured continued in the service is entitled for the compensation for the reimbursement of salary loss and also in the head of pain and suffering, medical expenses, incidental expenses and loss of amenities and discomfort. Mohammed Sufiyan vs Raju C on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133237852/ 8 In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 9621-2018 between Sri. Govinda Karvi V/s. Sri. Tharanath and Another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the absence of medical evidence to show the disability awarded the global compensation. In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 22898-2010 connected with MFA No.22899- 2010 between The Branch Manager, Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. P. Shaik Basha wherein it is held that when the minor injuries are sought to be projected as a serious injuries, they are not entitled for the compensation. In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 5905-2006 between Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Shivanna and another, the Hon'ble High Court when the false certificate is given by the doctors while assessing the disability has to be rejected and proper investigation has to be done by the investigating agency in respect of the accident. In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka 1449-2023 connected with 3330-2023 between Iffco Tokio Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., V/s. Smt. Jayashree and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that when there is no exact evidence to show that due to the injuries the petitioner has lost working capacity, the consideration of loss of future income due to disability does not arise. By relying on the above quoted judgments, the learned counsel for the respondent no.2 insurance company argued that in this case, no future loss of income is awarded.
